items.title: Ernie Cagnolatti Interview, 1961-04-05
items.q: He played about three years with, uh, with Paul, about, uh, David Mathon. David Mathon, yeah. And David, sorry to lose him. I mean, he was such a, he was such a great drummer.

ctx.x: He was a musical and clarinet. And sing like King Cole. When I went to the opera house. But couldn't play harmonica. When I went to the opera house, he said, you don't have no drum. He said, no, you ain't. Got last that drum, you can't come from here. I said, okay, I bought a, that white set big footbill hat and put him on it. Well, he tore, boy, the street from Jersey. Every night he, every night he's getting better.
He played about three years with, uh, with Paul, about, uh, David Mathon. David Mathon, yeah. And David, sorry to lose him. I mean, he was such a, he was such a great drummer.

About one more minute left here. About another minute left on the tape. Is there anything else you want to say before we quit? About, uh, either any of the jobs you've played. Or any of your favorite musicians. Or anything at all that you want to add to the story. I know that you have Shots Madison down there.
